messages:
Soojin Lee: Dropping updated marketplace headline/value props for review. Goal: clearer “why Redwood” + procurement-friendly language, without losing dev-first. Doc (working): https://drive.google.com/redwood/marketplace/aws-listing-copy-draft

Soojin Lee: Current headline options:
A) “High-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”
B) “Production-grade LLM inference: lower latency, lower cost, flexible deployment.”
C) “Developer-first LLM inference with enterprise-grade controls.”

Camila Reyes: Thanks. B is strongest for outcomes, but feels a little generic. Can we anchor on “inference platform” + “predictable”/“reliable”?

Ben Carter: +1. Also keyword density matters for marketplace search (AWS + GCP). “LLM inference” and “model serving” should be in first ~120 chars.

Soojin Lee: Noted. What about:
“Predictable LLM inference and model serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

Evelyn Hart: I like “predictable,” but let’s make sure we’re not implying hard guarantees on latency. “Predictable performance” is okay; “guaranteed latency” is not.

Nikhil Sharma: From product POV: we should mention “routing + fallbacks” and “observability” somewhere, but probably not in the headline.

Camila Reyes: Agree. Headline should be simple. Maybe:
“Production LLM inference with flexible deployment (hosted, dedicated, private).”

Ben Carter: Slight tweak for search: include “model serving” explicitly. Some buyers search “model serving platform” not “inference.”

Soojin Lee: Okay, proposal for headline:
“Production LLM inference & model serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

Camila Reyes: That reads well. Can we shorten? Some marketplaces truncate aggressively.

Ben Carter: AWS “Product title” can be longer, but the first clause is what shows in cards. If we front-load “Production LLM inference” we’re good.

Kira Thompson: Also for buyer comprehension: “hosted, dedicated, private” might need a parenthetical like “VPC/on‑prem” somewhere (maybe first paragraph).

Soojin Lee: Got it. Here are revised value prop bullets (for the listing hero section):
1) “Low-latency, high-throughput inference optimized for production workloads.”
2) “Deployment flexibility: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on‑prem) options.”
3) “Operational tooling: token-level cost + latency breakdowns, rollouts, and automated fallback policies.”

Camila Reyes: Bullet 1: “optimized for production workloads” is fine. Maybe add “reliable” or “SLA options” but careful not to overpromise.

Evelyn Hart: +1. “SLA-backed” belongs only where it’s actually true (Dedicated / certain SKUs). We can say “SLA options available” or “premium SLA add-on available” if that’s accurate.

Nikhil Sharma: Bullet 3 is great but a little dense. Suggest: “Observability + rollouts: cost/latency analytics, canaries, A/B tests, and fallbacks.”

Ben Carter: Keywords list suggestion (AWS/GCP):
- LLM inference
- model serving
- embeddings
- GPU inference
- open models
- throughput
- latency
- VPC deployment
- on-prem
- enterprise procurement

Ben Carter: Avoid “SOC2” as a keyword unless we’re sure the listing policy allows compliance terms in keywords. Some reviewers get picky; better in Security/FAQ attachment.

Soojin Lee: Good call. For keywords, I’ll keep compliance out and put “security controls” in body copy.

Camila Reyes: Also avoid “best-in-class” / “#1” phrasing. Reviewers hate superlatives.

Soojin Lee: Yep. Updating language to avoid absolutes.

Soojin Lee: How do we feel about this opening paragraph (first 2 sentences):
“Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for production LLM inference and model serving. Run and optimize open models with consistent performance across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem).”

Kira Thompson: That’s strong. Maybe add a third sentence that signals “procurement-ready” without saying “enterprise-grade” 3x:
“Purchase via AWS/GCP Marketplace to align spend with your cloud commit and simplify invoicing.”

Ben Carter: +1, and we can add UTM’d link to “Marketplace onboarding” docs once live.

Evelyn Hart: Make sure “consistent performance” isn’t read as a guarantee across all models/hardware. Maybe “consistent developer experience and operational tooling” is safer.

Soojin Lee: Good point. Revised:
“...with a consistent developer experience and operational tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem).”

Camila Reyes: Approved from my side. :thumbsup: Add a short “Why buy via marketplace” section with 3 bullets, and we’re in good shape.

Soojin Lee: Great. I’ll push edits into the draft today + update the keyword list. Next pass I’ll share the “card view” version (short description) for truncation review.
